draft.title: Tree diagrams for two events
card: A tree diagram shows the outcomes of one step as branches. Each outcome then splits into new branches for the second step.
Follow one path from the start to the end of the branches. That path is one combined outcome, such as red then blue.
To list every combined outcome, follow every path. The number of paths is the number of outcomes in the first step \(\times\) the number in the second.
When every path is equally likely, each combined outcome has probability \(\frac{1}{\text{number of paths}}\). For two coin tosses there are 4 paths, so \(P(HH) = \frac{1}{4}\).
draft.remember: Each path through the branches is one combined outcome.

a.q: A fair coin is tossed twice. Counting the paths on the tree diagram, what is \(P(HT)\)?
a.why: The tree has \(2 \times 2 = 4\) equally likely paths: HH, HT, TH and TT. HT is one of them, so \(P(HT) = \frac{1}{4}\). Using \(\frac{1}{2}\) counts only the first toss.
a.clue: Count all the paths, then count the paths that match.

b.q: Sam picks one of three cards marked A, B and C, then tosses a coin. Which list shows every outcome on the tree?
opts: AH, AT, BH, BT, CH, CT
AA, BB, CC, HH, TT, HT
b.why: Each of the 3 cards splits into heads and tails, giving \(3 \times 2 = 6\) paths. The list with only 4 outcomes leaves out card C. Each path must have one card result then one coin result.
b.clue: Follow each card's branches to both coin results.

b.best: AH, AT, BH, BT, CH, CT
